subject: Request: Executive approval for exceptional Hosted API concession - Summit Health
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Summit Health - ask for executive discount approval (30%)

Kimberly,

Quick one — Summit Health (Sarah Patel) got us to an ROE this morning that asks for a 30% unit-rate reduction off our standard Hosted API list for the first 12 months in exchange for a 3-region committed volume (18 months ramp, $8.5M ARR run-rate by year 2). They also want a 60-day invoice payment term and a note about data residency (US-only).

Rationale: Strategic anchor customer for payer integrations in Northeast, high likelihood of logo/reference + multi-product expansion if we accept. Risks: deeper-than-standard concession, longer payment terms.

Attached: summary commit (SummitHealth_MA_Pipeline_Commit.xlsx) and my annotated term sheet.

Ask: Can we get executive signoff for a 30% concession on Hosted API for the committed band (months 1–12)? If not full signoff, what is the maximum % we can safely approve today to keep momentum?

Thanks — I can jump on a quick sync if useful.

— Jordan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com] | +1-415-555-0193
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T10:34:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Summit Health - ask for executive discount approval (30%)

Jordan —

Thanks for the context and the attachment. A few quick questions before I escalate:

- Can you confirm the committed tokens/month bands and the proposed unit tieouts? The attachment is helpful but I need the exact tier math (sheet tab: committed_band).
- Is this a prepay or invoice model? You mention 60-day; finance will push back.
- What are the minimum acceptable outcomes from Summit we should lock in (case study, reference, fair-use clause)?

Mina — please jump in with the finance risk here (DSO impact / prepay required?). Ben — is a 30% concession within the range you want to take to exec? If not, what would you approve for a rep to sign today (if any)?

I'll prepare a short exec memo for the leadership thread — include the business impact and fallback concession band.

-Kim
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Summit Health - ask for executive discount approval (30%)

Kim / Jordan —

Reviewed the numbers. Key points:

- DSO: 60-day invoice terms materially increase working capital exposure given the scale; we'd prefer a 30-day standard or prepay cadence for the first 6 months. We can model a compromise: 45-day invoice with an early-pay discount tied to 15 days.
- Margin: A 30% unit discount drops our contribution margin below the threshold we use for strategic concessions (~35% contribution). We could support up to a 22% concession if they accept prepay for months 1–6 or provide a legally-binding case study and reference clause (preferred).
- Controls: Add a 6-month performance checkpoint (usage and quality) that allows us to revert to standard pricing if usage patterns are not met. Also require redline to include explicit data residency clause (US-only) and SOC 2 appendix.

Attachments: Summit_Contract_Redline.docx (redlines visible).

If Leadership wants to push to 30% they should agree to one of the following: (1) prepay for months 1–6 for the committed band, or (2) escrow payment guarantee, or (3) extended onboarding fee to offset ramp costs. Without one of those, I recommend capping concession at 22%.

-Mina
Senior Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Summit Health - ask for executive discount approval (30%) -- Exec note

Team —

I reviewed Mina's analysis and Jordan's go-to-market rationale. I'm comfortable granting an exception up to 25% for the committed 12-month band provided we get one of the following:

1) Prepay for months 1–6 covering at least 60% of the committed volume, OR
2) 45-day terms plus a signed reference & marketing agreement, OR
3) A $150k onboarding fee to offset first-half ramp costs.

If Summit accepts any of the above we can proceed with the 25% concession today; anything above 25% requires CEO-level signoff (we should prepare a one-pager for exec review if Jordan believes 30% is still necessary).

Kim — please send the memo to the exec thread with Mina's modeled P&L and include the two attachments/HubSpot link. Jordan — please push Summit for prepay or the reference ask and confirm which path they prefer.

Ben Carter
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
-- Forwarded message --
From: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@summithealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T07:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Hosted API pilot

Jordan —

Appreciate the proposal. Summit Health is ready to commit to a multi-region pilot and a firm volume ramp if we can get a 30% introductory rate to help offset integration costs. Procurement is flexible on payment cadence if it helps (we can do 45-day), but marketing/reference and a case study are non-negotiable for us.

We expect a signed statement of work within 10 business days once terms agreed.

— Sarah Patel
Director, Strategic Partnerships | Summit Health
sarah.patel@summithealth.com

[Attachment: Summit MSA summary.pdf]
